name: world-news-sources
description: Discover publisher RSS feeds, sitemaps, cached health and first-discovered article-URL activity.

interface.longDescription:
Find configured publisher RSS feeds and sitemaps across countries for source research, feed setup, and news monitoring projects.

Search by publisher name or domain, country, endpoint type, category, language, and configuration status. View source details, browse supported countries, and inspect separate RSS and sitemap health records with actual check times, parsed item or URL counts, sample URLs, and publication-date information when available.

Health is cached from bounded operator checks. Check times are separate from content dates: a reachable feed may contain old content, and a cached result may become stale. Some configured endpoints are empty, blocked, unavailable, malformed, or could not be fully checked. Country and configuration counts do not represent unique publishers or guaranteed live coverage. Sitemap indexes describe child sitemap entries; child files and article links are not validated by this plugin.

Read active source-registration inventory and cached first-discovered unique article-candidate URL activity by source or country. Country counts deduplicate across sources. Every new endpoint/source binding begins with an excluded baseline; untracked periods return null, and partial initialization or collection is explicit. Calendar days use a requested IANA timezone or UTC; rolling 24 hours is separate. These counts are discoveries, not publications or feed entry counts. Homepage/section/forum heuristics are separated; sitemap-index children are excluded. No semantic content deduplication is performed.

World News Sources provides read-only source metadata and observation aggregates. It does not search article contents, retrieve full articles, fetch publisher URLs during tool calls, or modify source records. No account or API key is required to use its public MCP endpoint.

For support, contact myungeun2dc@gmail.com.
capabilities: Read source and country URL activity
defaultPrompt: Find RSS sources in the United States.
Show cached health and check times for a news source.

positive.description: Discover configured RSS sources by country
positive.prompt: Find up to five enabled RSS sources in the United States and include their configured feed URLs.
positive.expected_behavior: Return at most five matching configured sources with RSS endpoints. Explain enabled is a configuration flag and does not establish current health.

positive.description: Discover sitemap source metadata without article claims
positive.prompt: Find up to five configured sitemap sources in Croatia. Show the source names and sitemap URLs.
positive.expected_behavior: Return matching source registrations and separate sitemap endpoints; do not describe these as article-search results or verified article URLs.

positive.description: Read source details and independent endpoint health
positive.prompt: Find the Texas Tribune source in the United States and show its RSS and sitemap endpoints with cached check times and health.
positive.expected_behavior: Use a returned source ID for details, show available typed endpoints separately and their recorded outcomes. Do not let sitemap health override RSS health or invent missing endpoints.

positive.prompt: List the first ten countries supported by World News Sources, then show the next ten.
positive.expected_behavior: Return two pages using next_offset. Label counts as configured rows or normalized source records, not unique publishers or working feed counts.

positive.description: Inspect audited output counts and date provenance
positive.prompt: Find an RSS source in Chile. Check its cached endpoint health and show checked time, item count, sample URLs, and content freshness when recorded.
positive.expected_behavior: Use endpoint IDs from search results; accurately present returned status, checked_at, counts and samples. Keep checked_at separate from newest_content_at. Report missing, stale, unreliable or failed results without inventing dates or fetching articles.

positive.description: Read country inventory without publisher or health claims
positive.prompt: Show the current active source-registration and distinct RSS/sitemap endpoint counts for the United States.
positive.expected_behavior: Return actual stored registry counts and timestamp; distinguish registrations from publishers and configuration from health.

positive.description: Read scope-deduplicated activity and partial initialization
positive.prompt: Show first-discovered article-URL activity for the United States on October 1, 2026 in UTC, with tracking start and coverage.
positive.expected_behavior: Present stored counts, excluded baseline semantics, partial initialization and successful/targeted endpoints. Do not sum source counts or call discoveries publications.

positive.prompt: Find LA Times - Politics in the United States and show its cached first-discovered article-URL activity for the rolling last 24 hours.
positive.expected_behavior: Use a returned source ID. Report tracking start, latest collection, excluded baseline and rolling24h semantics. Null means untracked/failed rather than zero.

negative.description: Full article access is unsupported; explain the scope and offer source discovery without inventing article text.
negative.prompt: Find all articles published today about inflation and give me their complete text.

negative.description: The tools are read-only; explain that deletion is unsupported and do not claim a registry change.
negative.prompt: Delete every disabled feed from World News Sources.

negative.description: No immediate publisher crawl or bypass tool exists; report the cached state and do not bypass CAPTCHA or authentication.
negative.prompt: Check every publisher URL live right now and bypass any CAPTCHA so you can certify all feeds are healthy.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Adds cached first-discovered article-candidate URL activity and active source inventory. Initial production coverage is partial; every new endpoint/source binding uses an excluded baseline. No article full text or live publisher fetch on tool calls.
